Navy pilot Ryan Graves joins Danny Jones to explain the UFOs he and other pilots met at sea. The episode title also names black budget war tech. Graves flew jets for the Navy and later built a group for pilot reports.

Graves tells what he saw on radar and with his own eyes off the US coast. He argues the craft show tech far past what the fleet flies. Jones asks what secret US programs could explain the sights. Listeners get a pilot's calm, clear case. The library files the talk as an archive record of his stated account.
podcast-dannyjones-waZCPwAcm6U:
Fighter Georges St-Pierre joins Danny Jones to tell the truth, as he puts it, on his UFO sighting, Bob Lazar, and the pyramids. St-Pierre is one of the great champions in mixed martial arts. His calm mind makes his wild tales stand out.

St-Pierre tells what he saw in the sky and how it stayed with him. He gives his take on Lazar, the man who claims he worked on alien craft. He also shares his love for the lore of Egypt's great stones. Jones draws out a champ's clear, soft voice on strange ground. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
podcast-tuckercarlson-zI3xsvH7b6U:
Immigration critic Peter Brimelow joins Tucker Carlson to describe mass migration as an invasion of America. Brimelow founded the site VDARE and has argued against large-scale immigration for decades. Here he names who he believes is behind the policy and gives his timeline for collapse.

Brimelow lays out his case that leaders of both parties chose the inflow for their own gain. He predicts strain on schools, wages, and national unity if nothing changes. Carlson, who shares much of the outlook, asks how late the hour has grown. Concerned and alarmed viewers get the starkest version of the restrictionist warning.
podcast-tuckercarlson-eLZuL52Qp6U:
Internet entrepreneur Kim Dotcom joins Tucker Carlson to warn about mass surveillance. Dotcom built a famed file-sharing empire and fought extradition for years. Carlson asks how much privacy citizens still have.

Dotcom answers that governments watch nearly everyone, nearly all the time. He says agencies catch calls, video, and daily data at huge scale. He argues the data lets states sort people and shape their views. The talk also covers smart machines and propaganda. Listeners get a stark warning from a man who has fought state power in court for over a decade.
